chunks: ʿAlī ibn Ibrāhīm, from his father, from Ibn Abī ʿUmayr, from Jamīl, from Muḥammad ibn Muslim, from Abū Jaʿfar عليه السلام, who said:
If a woman sees blood before ten days, then it is from the first menstruation; and if it is after ten days, then it is from the forthcoming menstruation.

Then he said, may Allah the Exalted support him: It is appropriate for the menstruating woman to perform the wudu of salat (prayer) at its times and sit to one side of her place of prayer, then praise Allah, magnify Him, declare His oneness, and glorify Him for the measure of the duration of her salat (prayer) at the time of every salat (prayer).

key_terms.الدَّمَ: blood seen by the woman, used here for legal classification
key_terms.الْحَيْضَةِ الْأُولَى: the first menstruation, meaning the earlier menstrual period
key_terms.الْحَيْضَةِ الْمُسْتَقْبَلَةِ: the forthcoming menstruation, meaning a new menstrual cycle
key_terms.عَشَرَةِ أَيَّامٍ: the ten-day interval that determines whether bleeding belongs to the earlier or later menstrual period
key_terms.وُضُوءَ الصَّلَاةِ: wudu performed in the manner of preparation for salat

ai.seo_question: How does Shia fiqh determine whether bleeding belongs to a previous menstruation or a new one, and what should a menstruating woman do at prayer times?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling on how to classify blood seen by a woman in relation to the ten-day period, distinguishing between continuation of a previous menstruation and the onset of a later one. It also recommends that a menstruating woman maintain devotional practice at prayer times through wudu, dhikr, and sitting in her place of worship for the duration of her usual salat.
